data.aeoQuickAnswer: Pitchside uses one or two ordinary phones as the football camera. Mount one phone near halfway for the simplest setup, or use two phones facing opposite goals for better coverage. The app processes suitable footage after full-time for supported stats, highlights and player output. The separate double-phone mount remains in development.
data.intro: Pitchside does not require a permanent football camera at the venue. The app is designed around footage from one or two ordinary phones, positioned to give a stable view of a 5-a-side, 6-a-side or 7-a-side pitch. The phone records the match. Pitchside processes suitable footage afterwards for supported stats, highlights and player output.

data.heroH1: Your phone is the camera. The setup decides what it sees.

contentBlocks.content: First decision: one phone or two?
One phone
Place one phone near halfway, above head height, in landscape orientation. Frame the complete playing area where possible.
Best for: Compact pitches, first tests and teams with one suitable device. Main risk: Players and events at the far end can become small or disappear behind other players. Setup effort: Lowest.
Two phones
Place both phones near halfway, with one facing each goal. Each phone covers one half more closely.

Best for: Wider small-sided pitches and stronger goal-area detail. Main risk: Two batteries, two storage checks and two files have to be managed. Setup effort: Higher, but this is the preferred Pitchside arrangement where practical.
Blind spots to check before kick-off
A mount cannot fix a poor position.
Walk the pitch and look for:

items: fencing that crosses the camera view;
substitutes standing directly in front of the phone;
a low angle that hides the ball behind players;
bright floodlights or sunlight pointing into the lens;
a goal area that sits outside the frame;
movement caused by wind, an unstable surface or an unsafe clamp;
notifications, incoming calls or storage limits that may interrupt recording.

contentBlocks.content: Record a short test clip and watch it from both ends of the pitch before the match begins.
The mount depends on the venue
There is no single safe mount for every cage, fence and touchline.
Fence clamp
Useful where the venue permits it and the fence gives a stable, unobstructed position. Check that the phone and clamp cannot fall towards players.
Tripod or light stand
Portable and adjustable, but it needs space, weight and protection from wind or contact. A tall stand should never be left unsecured.
Existing elevated surface
Only use a surface if the phone can be secured safely and the venue allows it. A loose phone balanced on a wall or bag is not a recording system.
The detailed phone recording guide should carry approved affiliate recommendations, checked prices and safety notes. This product page should remain focused on the Pitchside method.
The Pitchside double-phone mount
Pitchside is developing a mount for the preferred two-phone setup. The product is intended to make it easier to position two devices near halfway, with one facing each goal.
Do not publish compatibility, dimensions, materials, weather resistance, safety limits, price or delivery dates until they have been tested and approved.
The mount is a separate product from the app subscription. Buying or using a mount does not automatically include a Paid app plan unless Dave approves a bundle.
What makes this an AI football camera app?
The camera does not need to pan and follow the ball during the match. Pitchside works from the captured view after upload and uses the footage for the available analysis workflow.
That makes it different from a motorised phone tracker and from a dedicated panoramic camera. Each approach has trade-offs:

cells: The view framed by one or two phones
Low hardware barrier and player-focused output
Coverage depends on position and pitch size
A moving view that follows play
May not preserve the complete pitch view
Wide or full-field source, depending on system

What happens to the recording
After full-time, upload the footage through the available Pitchside workflow. The private beta processes suitable recordings and returns supported match output for review.
Processing can currently take up to 45 minutes. Read the complete football video analysis workflow.
App plans and mount pricing are separate
The app's Free plan includes one recording per month, Match Stats & Highlights, Leaderboards and Personal Stats.
The Paid plan includes one recording per week and Personal Clips for £4.99 weekly, £12.99 monthly or £99 annually.
The Pitchside double-phone mount price is not included in this draft. Add it only after preorder terms are approved.

faqs.answer: Pitchside is an app and analysis platform designed to work with suitable phone-recorded footage. A separate double-phone mount is in development.
faqs.question: Is Pitchside a camera or an app?
Do I need two phones?
faqs.answer: No. One phone can work when it clearly covers the complete small-sided pitch. Two phones are preferred when a single view loses too much detail.

faqs.question: Which phones are compatible?
faqs.answer: Publish a tested compatibility list before launch. Do not use broad “works with any phone” language unless the recording, upload and app requirements support it.

The fixed-phone Pitchside setup does not need to pan during the match. It records the framed view for post-match processing. Do not confuse this workflow with the earlier motorised tracking-mount concept unless that hardware is still part of the approved product.
